info.name: Geospatial Measurement API
info.description:
Upload a Shapefile (.zip) or KML file and get the area (m²) of every polygon and the length (m) of every line, measured after reprojecting to the UTM zone of each feature.

**Setup:** the `base_url` variable points at the hosted deployment. Change it to `http://localhost:8000` to test a local instance. `file_id` is filled in automatically when you run an upload request.

**Typical flow:** Health Check → Upload Shapefile or Upload KML → Get File Info (repeat until `COMPLETED`) → Get Measurements. If the hosted service has been idle it may need a moment to wake up, so the first request can be slow.

request.description:
Checks that the service is up and can reach its database (it runs `SELECT 1`).

**What to set:** nothing. Run this first; if the hosted service has been idle, it also wakes it up.

**What comes back:** `200` with the body below. If the database is unreachable you get `503` with `{"detail": "Database unavailable", "code": "DB_UNAVAILABLE"}`.

**Example response (200):**

```json
{
  "status": "ok"
}
```

Lists uploaded files, newest first, one page at a time.

**What to set:** `page` (1-based, default 1) and `page_size` (default 20, maximum 100) in the query params. Copy an `id` from the result into the `file_id` variable to inspect that file.

**What comes back:** `200` with the pagination totals and a compact entry per file. An empty database returns `total: 0` and an empty `items` list. `page_size` over 100 or `page` below 1 gives `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

**Example response (200):**

```json
{
  "page": 1,
  "page_size": 20,
  "total": 1,
  "total_pages": 1,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "8e4bcba8-dfcc-4609-b116-718620bb14b3",
      "filename": "survey.kml",
      "status": "COMPLETED",
      "feature_count": 3,
      "crs": "EPSG:4326",
      "created_at": "2026-10-08T23:25:24.191828Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

request.description:
Uploads a Shapefile packaged as a ZIP archive.

**What to set:** in the Body tab, click the `file` field and choose a file from your computer. Only a `.zip` that contains the Shapefile parts (`.shp`, `.shx`, `.dbf`) and a `.prj` that declares the CRS. Without a `.prj` the file fails with a message asking for one is accepted.

**What comes back:** `202 Accepted` straight away with status `PENDING`. Nothing has been measured yet: parsing runs in the background. The test script on this request saves the returned `id` into the `file_id` collection variable, so you can run **Get File Info** next and repeat it until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

**Example response (202):**

```json
{
  "id": "8e4bcba8-dfcc-4609-b116-718620bb14b3",
  "filename": "survey.kml",
  "status": "PENDING"
}
```

**Errors:** `400 INVALID_FILE_TYPE` (wrong extension or content), `400 EMPTY_FILE`, `413 FILE_TOO_LARGE` (limit is 50 MB by default), `422 CORRUPT_FILE` (not a valid ZIP, no `.shp` inside, or no `<kml>` element). Every error body is `{"detail": "...", "code": "..."}`.

request.description:
Uploads a KML file.

**What to set:** in the Body tab, click the `file` field and choose a file from your computer. Only a `.kml` file. KMZ is not supported. Every folder in the KML is read, and a folder that cannot be read is skipped and reported in `warnings` on Get File Info is accepted.

**What comes back:** `202 Accepted` straight away with status `PENDING`. Nothing has been measured yet: parsing runs in the background. The test script on this request saves the returned `id` into the `file_id` collection variable, so you can run **Get File Info** next and repeat it until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

**Example response (202):**

```json
{
  "id": "8e4bcba8-dfcc-4609-b116-718620bb14b3",
  "filename": "survey.kml",
  "status": "PENDING"
}
```

**Errors:** `400 INVALID_FILE_TYPE` (wrong extension or content), `400 EMPTY_FILE`, `413 FILE_TOO_LARGE` (limit is 50 MB by default), `422 CORRUPT_FILE` (not a valid ZIP, no `.shp` inside, or no `<kml>` element). Every error body is `{"detail": "...", "code": "..."}`.

Returns a file's status and metadata. This is the request to repeat after an upload.

**What to set:** the `file_id` collection variable (set automatically by the upload requests, or paste an id from List Files). The URL ends in a slash on purpose: without it the request matches no route and you get `404 NOT_FOUND`.

**What comes back:** `200` with the status, which moves `PENDING` → `PROCESSING` → `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. `feature_count` and `crs` are `null` until it completes. `error` explains a `FAILED` file. `warnings` lists parts of a `COMPLETED` file that were skipped. `crs` is `EPSG:<code>` only for an exact match, otherwise `CUSTOM:` followed by the start of its WKT. An unknown id gives `404 FILE_NOT_FOUND`; a malformed id gives `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

**Example response (200):**

```json
{
  "id": "8e4bcba8-dfcc-4609-b116-718620bb14b3",
  "filename": "survey.kml",
  "feature_count": 3,
  "crs": "EPSG:4326",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
  "error": null,
  "warnings": [],
  "file_size": 557,
  "created_at": "2026-10-08T23:25:24.191828Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-08T23:25:24Z"
}
```
